# AGENTS.md — `.github/` (release & CI footguns)

Auto-loaded when touching workflows/scripts here. Engine + version-matrix doctrine + commit/CHANGELOG rules live in the **root `AGENTS.md`** (always loaded). This file = release/publish/CI specifics only. Append surprises here when they're CI/release-scoped; root keeps the general meta-rule.

## Release flow & `main` promotion (MANUAL — SETTLED, do NOT "fix")
Releases are cut from `dev`, tagged `v*`. `main` is ONLY the JitPack `main-SNAPSHOT` surface + the ref `main`-tracking consumers follow — it LAGS by design and is advanced per release.
- **Promote `main` as an ATTENDED step after a successful *stable* publish**: `git push origin <tag>:main` (clean ff; the tag descends from `main`). Works because `main`'s protection keeps `required_signatures` + `required_linear_history` + push restricted to `art-shen`, but **`enforce_admins` is OFF** → the admin's signed ff is accepted WITHOUT the 7 required status contexts (6 `…/JDK*` + `pr-check`). A release/tag commit structurally NEVER carries those contexts, so it could never satisfy them — that's why a direct push is *rejected* while `enforce_admins` is on.
- **Pre-releases (`-alpha`/`-beta`/`-rc`, detected in `verify-release.sh`) must NOT move `main`.**
- `gh_release` creates the GitHub release as a **draft** (`create-github-release.sh` always `--draft`); the maintainer publishes it (`gh release edit <tag> --draft=false --latest`) in the SAME manual post-publish pass as the `main` ff. Both are deliberate outward-facing gates — artifacts are already live on Central + Portal by then, so the draft only holds the announcement.
- **The gate is against UNATTENDED CI automation, NOT agency.** The attended pass may be run by a human OR by an agent the user authorises per-release (explicit permission + request). An agent MAY publish/promote *when asked* — but NONE of it may be CI-wired to fire by itself.
- **There is deliberately NO automated promotion job.** A prior `promote_main` + `promote-main.sh` was removed: the CI bot isn't in `restrictions`, so it needed a `MAIN_PROMOTE_TOKEN` bypass actor to push protected `main`, and without it went red every release. Do NOT re-add an unattended job that toggles `enforce_admins` — an automated relax can leave `main` silently unprotected on failure.

## Publish verification (`release.yml` + `verify-*.sh`)
- **The publish step is the IRREVERSIBLE commit point; everything after it only reports.** Central + Portal publish are split into two SEQUENTIAL `gradlew` invocations (Central first), never one combined task list — both are `:plugin` tasks with no inter-dependency, so Gradle wouldn't guarantee their command-line order. Rationale is commented in `release.yml`.
- **Gradle Plugin Portal has ONE `description` field.** Plugin Publish Plugin sends one `description` from `gradlePlugin.plugins`; the Portal renders it in BOTH the top section and version card (top adds the website sentence). Do NOT put changelog/release-notes there. Portal metadata is SSOT-validated by `:plugin:verifyPluginPortalMetadata` against the `gradlePlugin` extension BEFORE publish — Maven POM correctness alone does NOT prove the Portal page.
- **The rendered Portal page is NOT a faithful echo of submitted metadata — never assert metadata literals against it.** Confirmed divergences (live 0.14.1 + 0.15.0): (1) source link always points at the repo DEFAULT branch (`…/tree/main`), never the per-version `vcsUrl` (`…/tree/v<version>`); (2) the Portal drops tags past its display limit (dropped `compose`). So `verify-plugin-portal-page.sh` verifies ONLY propagation — version page exists + marked `(latest)` — plus a stable repo-link anchor; it must NOT re-assert description/tags/source-URL literals.
- **Why the page check is its OWN non-gating job**: hardcoded literal checks sank v0.15.0's first publish — both publishes SUCCEEDED but the post-publish page check false-failed, skipping `gh_release` + promotion → a half-complete release. Defence: `verify_portal_page` runs in a separate job (`needs: publish_release`, NOT depended on by `gh_release`), so a Portal rendering/propagation hiccup can never again half-complete an already-published release.

## JitPack (lazy per-ref builds)
- **JitPack builds LAZILY per-ref — a release's JitPack surface is unbuilt (and the README badge stale) until the FIRST GET of that exact ref.** No "publish" step: the artifact for a tag/commit/`main-SNAPSHOT` doesn't exist until a request triggers a build (`jitpack.yml`: `./gradlew :plugin:publishToMavenLocal`, JDK 21). Passive observation CANNOT prove the JitPack path works; the badge (`/v/…svg`) shows the last *built* `ok` version, lagging until requested.
- **To verify AND warm it**: actively GET the consumer coordinate `https://jitpack.io/com/github/fluxo-kt/fluxo-kmp-conf/fluxo-kmp-conf/<commit|version>/…pom`. A **502 is a synchronous gateway timeout while the build runs on, NOT a failure** — confirm terminal `ok`/`Error` via the build API `https://jitpack.io/api/builds/com.github.fluxo-kt.fluxo-kmp-conf`.
- The tag, the README-pinned snapshot commit, and `main-SNAPSHOT` of the same HEAD are ONE source tree → ONE build result; verifying any one verifies all. The README snapshot example pins that commit by hand — bumping it is a deliberate MANUAL release step, not a defect to automate.

## CI scoping & review
- **Dependency Submission graph MUST be scoped to `runtimeClasspath` only** (`dependency-submission.yml`), never the whole graph. AGP/KGP/detekt are `compileOnly` → they + transitives (bundletool→jose4j, lint→bouncycastle, Develocity's log4j/jackson/opentelemetry/undertow) resolve in `compileClasspath` but NEVER ship. Submitting them floods Dependabot with build-only CVEs that mask real consumer-facing ones (the shipped surface = `implementation`/`api` = `runtimeClasspath`: spotless, detekt-gradle-plugin, jgit, okhttp). The include filter is anchored `^runtimeClasspath$` (can't partial-match `testRuntimeClasspath`/etc.); re-broadening it (e.g. `^(?!(classpath)).*`) silently re-leaks. Verify shipped deps via `dependencies/runtimeClasspath.txt`, not the full `buildEnvironment`.
- **Release secrets** (remote release via `vanniktech-mvn-publish`; SCM from `SCM_TAG`/`BUILD_NUMBER`, see `PropsAndEnv.kt`): Central Portal user-token (`MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME`, `MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD`), signing (`SIGNING_KEY`, `SIGNING_PASSWORD`, optional `SIGNING_KEY_ID`), Gradle Plugin Portal (`GRADLE_PUBLISH_KEY`, `GRADLE_PUBLISH_SECRET`). `verify-release.sh` blocks tag/version mismatch + pre-existing GitHub releases before publication.
- **AI review** runs automatically on maintainer PRs; Claude review also honours the `ai-review` label for explicit opt-in. CodeRabbit auto-reviews non-draft PRs and ignores bot authors via `.coderabbit.yaml`. Keep reusable review instructions in the `REVIEW_PROMPT` secret — NEVER in workflow YAML or GitHub variables.
- **macOS is the SLOWEST CI cell — size `build.yml` step `timeout-minutes` against IT, never ubuntu/windows.** macOS alone compiles the Apple/native (konan) KMP targets; an 18-min cap on the main `build assemble check` step red-flaked `macos/JDK23` on a commit green on every other cell + integration leg. Leave generous margin over the macOS native wall-time, below the 90-min job cap (a real hang must still trip).
- **Adding a `compat/matrix.tsv` row on a new JDK → install that JDK in `build.yml` integrationChecks + `release.yml`**, else compat fixtures fail loudly (the `jdkVersion` column is enforced — see root AGENTS.md *compatibilityTest* surprise for why).
